Medieval Halloween: Soul Cakes and Bells | History for Sleep

Premieres Fri 23 Oct at 5 PM ET (21:00 UTC) · About 1 hour 57 min · narrated slowly for sleep

Find it on our YouTube channel

The video goes public on the channel at the premiere time.

Medieval Halloween history for sleep: a calm, two-hour night on All Hallows' Eve in a late-medieval English village, with soul cakes, souling, and church bells rung all night for the souls of the dead.

The customs, bells and soul cakes are real, taken from old parish accounts and folklore records. Our village, Agnes, Wat and the ringers are imagined, and we say so whenever we are picturing rather than knowing.

This is a quiet bedtime documentary, narrated slowly to help you relax and drift off to sleep. No loud sounds, no sudden changes and no horror: just a soft voice, slow images, and faraway bells.

A note from Dreaming Ages

This episode began with one line in a parish account book from Heybridge in Essex, 1517: eightpence paid to John Gidney of Maldon "for a new bell-rope agenste Hallowmasse". A new rope, bought because the bells would be rung through the night for the souls of the dead. We followed that rope back into the village it served.
